heroHeadline: Junta Burns 4 Houses, Abducts 10 in Kani Township; Schools Campaign Escalates — 6+ Struck in 5 Weeks; AA Resumes Nat Yay Kan Assault; Maw Taung Advance Continues
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,931 of Myanmar's civil war (May 17, 2026), the Myanmar military junta escalated on multiple fronts: SAC jets struck Chaung Ma school in Kani Township, Sagaing Region, injuring four civilians, while ground troops simultaneously burned four houses and abducted ten residents in Thamin village — continuing a campaign that has displaced 30,900+ civilians from 44 Kani villages over two weeks. The Irrawaddy documented a systematic junta school-bombing escalation: at least six educational facilities struck in five weeks across Sagaing, Northern Shan State, and Karen State, with another warplane strike hitting the fortunately-closed Pauk Inn Myaing school in Sagaing on May 17. In Magway Region, the Arakan Army and allied resistance forces resumed their assault on the junta's Nat Yay Kan hilltop strategic base in Padan Township, reflecting the AA's expanding multi-front operations beyond Rakhine State. In Tanintharyi Region, three SAC columns continued pressing toward Maw Taung — KNLA Brigade 4's Thailand border crossing — with junta forces advancing within 15 miles of the town with daily airstrike support, as thousands of residents fled toward the Thai border. The May 17 events follow IIMM documentation (May 16) of 640+ airstrikes having killed or injured children since the 2021 coup, and the junta's simultaneous three-brigade offensive against KNLA, the Pauk Township displacement crisis (8,000+), and the Chin State humanitarian emergency (820+ civilians fled to India's Mizoram).
footerNote: Data sourced from AAPP, ACLED, UN OCHA, Irrawaddy, RFA, Myanmar Now, DVB, Al Jazeera, Mizzima, Human Rights Watch, Crisis Group, Myanmar Peace Monitor, MoeMaKa CDM News, IMNA / Mon News Agency, CPJ, Narinjara News, Global Arakan Network, Kachin Human Rights Watch, Aryan Age, NUG Ministry of Human Rights, Committee to Protect Journalists, Chin People's Union and Army (CPU/A), Burmese Rohingya Organisation UK (BROUK), IIMM (UN Independent Investigative Mechanism for Myanmar), and official NUG, KNU, KIA, AA, and PDF statements.
